decisive_items: Computed tomography angiography:  Image Title: Initial CT angiography  Image Description: Shows pulmonary embolism in the right pulmonary artery branching into segmental and lobar arteries, left segmental artery embolus, bilateral pleural effusions, evidence of right heart strain
ECG: T-wave inversions in anterior leads
response.rationale: CT angiography directly demonstrates bilateral pulmonary embolism with right heart strain, and the acute pleuritic pain, hypoxemia, and anterior T-wave inversions corroborate acute PE. Malignant pleural effusion is confirmed by cytology but is a secondary/comorbid finding that does not explain the right heart strain and acute PE syndrome.

rejected.why: Ovarian cancer history is the underlying risk factor/context, not the acute diagnosis; the malignant effusion is a manifestation but does not replace the acute PE diagnosis.
Malignant cells confirm a malignant pleural effusion, but this does not account for the CT-confirmed pulmonary embolism and right heart strain, which drive the acute presentation.
Hypoxemic respiratory failure is a physiologic consequence rather than a specific etiologic diagnosis; the cause is best explained by acute pulmonary embolism.
